bear: More investors doubt that the huge spending on AI will pay off, and the index leans heavily on tech companies.
Oil hit a six-month high because of the Middle East conflict, and airline stocks like United, Delta and American fell on worries about higher fuel costs.
Investors worry that higher oil prices will keep prices rising for everyone and push the Federal Reserve (the US central bank) to raise interest rates, which makes borrowing money cost more.
bull: 83% of the 111 S&P 500 companies that had reported so far earned more than experts predicted.
Few people were signing up for unemployment money, which shows the job market is holding steady.

briefs.headline: Exxon hits record highs after saying refining added $4.5 billion to profits
briefs.summary: In mid-October, Exxon gave an early look at its results for July to September. It said bigger refining margins, meaning the extra money it makes turning crude oil into fuels like gasoline, will add about $4.5 billion to profits compared with the quarter before. The stock rose 2% on October 17 to a record high of about $179, and it climbed more than 2% again on October 23 to around $183 as investors got ready for the full report. Lower oil prices and some one-time accounting effects will take back part of that gain.
bull: Refining margins are expected to add $4.5 billion to profits in the July–September quarter, more than double what the fuels business earned the quarter before.
A Goldman Sachs analyst said the early numbers point to profit of about $4.10 per share, higher than the $3.87 many experts expected.
Exxon owns oil fields and also refineries, so strong refining made up for lower oil prices. The company keeps paying a $1.03 per share dividend, a cash payment to shareholders, every quarter.
bear: Lower oil prices are expected to cut about $1.3 billion from profits in Exxon's oil-drilling business, and the chemicals business faces a $600 million hit.
Exxon expects $2.5 billion in negative 'timing effects', meaning accounting changes that make this quarter's reported profit look lower.
Wells Fargo lowered its rating on the stock, and one market expert warned the rally may have gone too far and could reverse quickly if results disappoint.

briefs.summary: Johnson & Johnson reported its July-to-September results on October 13. Sales were $25.4 billion, up 5.9% from a year earlier, and profit per share beat what experts expected. On October 22 the stock rose 3.48% after good real-world results for its heart-rhythm devices, and because investors moved money into steady healthcare companies on a day when the wider market fell.
bull: J&J's medicine business grew about 8%, helped by strong sales of its cancer drugs and Tremfya, a drug for immune diseases.
An experimental prostate cancer pill, taken once a day, shrank or cleared tumors in many patients in an early test. The results were shared on October 24.
Most experts who follow the stock rate it positively, and Wells Fargo raised its guess for where the price could go to $287.
bear: J&J's profit by strict accounting rules fell sharply because of about $7 billion in one-time costs. Most of that came from a proposed deal to settle lawsuits over talc baby powder, plus costs of buying companies.
The medical device business grew only about 2.5%, held back by weak sales outside the US and at its Abiomed heart-pump unit.

Erste Group lowered its rating to 'hold' (meaning wait and see) because the stock already looks expensive compared with how much the company earns. Even after this week's gain, the stock is down about 5% over the past month.

bull: KFC is switching about 3,700 US restaurants from Pepsi to Coca-Cola drinks, so Coca-Cola wins a big customer from its main rival.
On October 16, the bank Barclays raised its price target (its guess of what the stock could be worth) from $93 to $98, and UBS set its target at $104.
The stock reached an all-time high on October 22, up about 34% from a year earlier.
bear: One analysis said the stock may be overpriced compared with what the company is really worth.
The stock is close to its highest price of the year, so a weak earnings report next week could hurt it.
KFC won't start switching drinks until January 2027, so the deal won't bring in sales right away.

Investors are nervous about how long the AI data center building boom will last, and about higher interest rates and oil prices.
